correctness.rationale: Exact charge conservation factors the field-dependent Gibbs operator as a two-sided product of invertible positive local filters around the zero-field Gibbs operator. Partial transpose turns this into an invertible Hermitian congruence, so Sylvester's law of inertia preserves every positive, negative and zero eigenvalue count. The spin-one XXZ plus single-ion model satisfies the conservation law exactly, and the packaged exact-rational checker verifies the exchange transitions and partial-transpose/filter identity.

originality.rationale: Selected-parameter field-independent negativity thresholds and a pure-biquadratic special case are prior, and invertible-local-filter theory is prior. The accepted novelty is limited to the exact Gibbs-to-local-filter congruence for any conserved additive charge and its consequence that the entire partial-transpose inertia, including all zero-crossing temperatures, is independent of every finite uniform field. Focused published-finding corpus searches and inspection of the closest spin-one full texts did not locate that universal statement.
residual_risks: The congruence proof is short and may have appeared implicitly under different terminology such as SLOCC filtering of Gibbs states; focused alias searches did not locate such a statement.
The 2021 source already states the final threshold independence for selected spin-one parameters, so only the universal all-coupling/full-inertia upgrade is claimed as original.
PPT is not sufficient for separability in 3x3; the theorem is deliberately limited to PPT/NPT and negativity support.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a selected-parameter field-independent threshold observation and one own-ledger special case to a reusable structural theorem valid for the full anisotropic spin-one parameter space and, more generally, any finite-dimensional additive-charge-conserving bipartite Hamiltonian. It additionally fixes every partial-transpose zero-crossing temperature, explaining field-independent kink locations and singular positive-temperature entanglement above field-polarized zero-temperature phases without parameter-by-parameter spectral calculations.
